source_refs.note: Exercise 9.2, Question 1 (book p. 272); the book prints no answers for Exercise 9.2; answers checked with sympy and the solution book

blocks.explanation:
A proof with numbers: two \(\sin^{-1}\) angles on the left, one \(\cos^{-1}\) on the right.
Plan: write both left angles in \(\cos^{-1}\) form (right triangles), then add them with formula (iii).
steps:
Given: \(\sin^{-1}\frac{7}{25}\) and \(\sin^{-1}\frac{15}{17}\).
To prove: their sum is \(\cos^{-1}\frac{87}{425}\).
Method: the answer is a \(\cos^{-1}\), so use formula (iii): \(\cos^{-1}x + \cos^{-1}y = \cos^{-1}\left(xy - \sqrt{(1-x^{2})(1-y^{2})}\right)\). First write each angle as a \(\cos^{-1}\).

Write \(\sin^{-1}\frac{7}{25}\) as a \(\cos^{-1}\)
\[\alpha = \sin^{-1}\tfrac{7}{25},\quad \sin\alpha = \tfrac{7}{25}\]
\[\cos\alpha = \sqrt{1 - \tfrac{49}{625}} = \sqrt{\tfrac{576}{625}}\]
\[= \tfrac{24}{25}\]
\[\alpha = \cos^{-1}\tfrac{24}{25}\]
Why: \(\sin^{2}\alpha + \cos^{2}\alpha = 1\). The sine is positive, so \(\alpha\) is in \(\left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\), where cosine is positive; that is also where \(\cos^{-1}\frac{24}{25}\) lies, so it is the same angle.

Write \(\sin^{-1}\frac{15}{17}\) as a \(\cos^{-1}\)
\[\beta = \sin^{-1}\tfrac{15}{17},\quad \sin\beta = \tfrac{15}{17}\]
\[\cos\beta = \sqrt{1 - \tfrac{225}{289}} = \sqrt{\tfrac{64}{289}}\]
\[= \tfrac{8}{17}\]
\[\beta = \cos^{-1}\tfrac{8}{17}\]
Why: the same reasoning (8, 15, 17 is a Pythagorean triple).

Apply formula (iii) with \(x = \frac{24}{25},\ y = \frac{8}{17}\)
\[\sqrt{1-x^{2}} = \tfrac{7}{25},\quad \sqrt{1-y^{2}} = \tfrac{15}{17}\]
\[\text{L.H.S} = \cos^{-1}\tfrac{24}{25} + \cos^{-1}\tfrac{8}{17}\]
\[= \cos^{-1}\left(\tfrac{24}{25}\cdot\tfrac{8}{17} - \tfrac{7}{25}\cdot\tfrac{15}{17}\right)\]
Why: the square roots are just the sines we started with. Formula (iii) needs \(x + y \ge 0\), which is true.

Check
\[\sin^{-1}\tfrac{7}{25} + \sin^{-1}\tfrac{15}{17} \approx 0.2838 + 1.0808\]
\[= 1.3646\]
\[\cos^{-1}\tfrac{87}{425} \approx 1.3646\ \checkmark\]
Why: a calculator in radian mode gives the same angle on both sides.
